newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav, Macedonian copper mines sign deal - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav, Macedonian copper mines sign deal - paper.

text.p: Yugoslavia's largest mining and smelting complex Rudarsko Topionicarski Basen (RTB) Bor has renewed cooperation with Macedonia's Bucim copper mine, the Belgrade daily Politika reported on Tuesday.

"Around 45,000-50,000 tonnes of copper concentrate from Bucim will be processed each year in Bor's smelters," deputy director of RTB Bor's smeltery and refinery Blazo Lekovski was quoted by the paper as saying.
Lekovski said the arrangement would raise Bor's production of copper by around 7,000 tonnes, while substantial quantities of silver and gold would also be produced.
No one at RTB Bor was immediately available for comment.
According to company figures released last month, RTB Bor produced 33,700 tonnes of copper concentrate and 65,000 tonnes of cathode copper from January to August.
In the same period, nearly nine million tonnes of copper ore were extracted from its mines.
The agreement with Bucim mine will secure full engagement of RTB Bor's smelting capacities and earnings of around $6 million, Lekovski said.
RTB Bor and Bucim copper mines also signed a deal for the servicing of Bucim's dumper trucks and other mining equipment in Bor's workshops. The value of the deal is around $600,000.
RTB Bor planned to produce 125,000 tonnes of cathode copper in 1996, including 74,000 tonnes from its own raw materials.
The complex's total refining capacity is around 170,000 tonnes of cathode copper.
